clue.text: Kitchen surface perhaps, useful to prophet taking heroin …

indicators.note: taking something away from the prophet's name means removing a letter from it

blocks.note: something useful to a task is good for it
Micah is a minor prophet of the Old Testament
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A worktop of some sort would suit a prophet who has a heroin habit, the ellipsis promising more on drugs to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking heroin' suggests an addict, but here the prophet is taking the H away from his own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Formica is a trademarked plastic laminate commonly used for worktops, so it is an example of a kitchen surface.

clue.text: Mad French caper

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French
an antic is a playful or silly caper

explanation.surface: A wild escapade carried out in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frantic is wild with worry or excitement, so mad in the sense of frenzied.

clue.text: Flower discernible in superior honey

indicators.note: something discernible in a phrase can be seen sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A blossom can be detected in premium honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is a flow-er, a river, as is common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river of Switzerland and France, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: It turns out Charlie’s left you at eastern entrance

indicators.note: Charlie having left means that letter has gone away from the phrase

blocks.note: 'in fact' is what you say when something turns out to be so
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
text-speak spelling of you
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that Charlie walked out on them at the eastern doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb en-TRANCE, to captivate. IN FACT loses its C, then U, AT and E follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate someone is to inspire foolish passion in them, much as to entrance is to hold them spellbound.

clue.text: Quite an upset from long ago

indicators.note: an upset turns things over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Something caused a considerable disturbance a long time back.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique object or custom dates from a much earlier period, so it comes from long ago.

clue.text: … E.g. Gandhi, taking half of heroin etc through biro

indicators.note: keeping only half of a word means dropping the other half of its letters
something running through another item sits inside it

blocks.note: Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint, the biro being its British generic name
heroin and its relatives are opiates

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across: Gandhi as a figure who took heroin and wrote with a ballpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of OPIATE, OPI, goes through BIC. Gandhi is the 1982 film about the Indian leader, not the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandhi is a film telling the life story of a real person, which is exactly what a biopic is.

clue.text: A date in March to beware – and time, that is

blocks.clueFragment: A date in March to beware
blocks.note: the soothsayer in Julius Caesar warns him to beware the Ides of March, the 15th
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A warning about the Ides of March, Caesar's fatal day, with a note about time.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase abbreviated i.e., meaning 'that is' when restating something.

clue.text: A child bearing large staff

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per
a son is a child
north-east is a compass bearing
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A youngster carrying a big stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a rod the child is carrying, but it means the people employed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the employees of an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Where you might get buns or tea outside

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
'or else' offers the alternative

explanation.surface: A café offer: buns, or else a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a sticky currant bun named after the London district of Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is the place that gave its name to the Chelsea bun, so it is where buns might be had.

clue.text: Art bold enough to be noticed in calendar – estimable!

indicators.note: something noticed in the words is spotted sitting among their letters

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A piece of art daring enough to be spotted in a fine calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is not painting but the old second-person 'thou art'; thou darest is the archaic form of you dare.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Thou darest' and 'thou art bold enough' are archaic equivalents, both addressing someone with courage.

clue.text: Plenty of time is lost or reserved

indicators.note: something lost has gone missing, so a letter disappears from the phrase

blocks.note: plenty of means a lot of
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Either a great deal of time gets wasted or it is set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof keeps their distance and is cool and reserved in manner.

clue.text: Creature such as bird in part

blocks.note: a toad is a creature
e.g. means for example, such as
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: An animal resembling a bird in some respects.
explanation.definitionFit: 'To a degree' means to some extent, partly, which is what 'in part' says.

clue.text: Queen’s snotty ‘wit’ disrupted parlour game

indicators.note: things disrupted are thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A haughty royal's attempt at humour spoils a drawing-room amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty Questions is a guessing game traditionally played indoors in the parlour, asking yes-or-no questions.

clue.text: First of drivers leaves taxi rank sign for Savoy?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, singled out here to be removed
a letter that leaves goes away from the word that held it

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
a badge shows military rank
the opening letter of drivers

explanation.surface: A cabbie quits the rank outside London's Savoy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy looks like the hotel with its taxi rank; the question mark flags a savoy, a crinkly-leaved cabbage.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoy is a variety of cabbage, so the clue defines by example.

clue.text: As a young man in the East End, don’t play so tough

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop their aitches, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: an instruction to act less tough: be hard less

explanation.surface: Advice to a young man from London's East End to stop acting the hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney accent of London's East End drops the H, turning be hard less into be 'ard less.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth too young to grow facial hair is beardless, so the word describes someone as a young man.

clue.text: Bottom attracts me; breast’s an interesting alternative initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

blocks.note: tit is slang for breast
taken as written
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A risqué line about being drawn to someone's backside, with a cheeky aside on breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' is not a backside but Nick Bottom the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, whom the fairy queen is bewitched into loving.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania, queen of the fairies, is enchanted to dote on Bottom, so she could say he attracts her.

clue.text: Scrap with the French getting wind up?

definitions.text: Scrap with the French getting wind up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
la is a French word for 'the'
a fart is breaking wind

explanation.surface: A fight with the French in which someone gets the wind up, that is, takes fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as the definition: a scrap with the French that put the wind up them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Trafalgar in 1805 was a naval fight between Britain and the combined French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: Struggle to accept old misfortune

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to try is to struggle or strive
aged means old

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a past calamity is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a disastrous event, a great misfortune.

clue.text: Germans bombed Euston after Tuesday

indicators.note: something bombed is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: T is an abbreviation for Tuesday
the fodder letters

explanation.surface: German bombers hit Euston station, the London rail terminus, the day after Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teutons were an ancient Germanic tribe, and Teuton is used loosely for any German.

clue.text: In 8 maybe I agree, there’s no end to rowdy, peevish type of politics

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: yah is the posh Sloane way to say yes, as heard in a smart district like 8 down
a rowdy, a rough lout, is a boor

explanation.surface: A Chelsea voter grumbles agreement that rowdy, petty politics never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer at 8 down, the affluent London area whose upper-class residents say 'yah' for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah-boo politics is the childish jeering and point-scoring of adversarial debate, petulant and peevish.

clue.text: Their predictions are unclear? Wrong – so clear!

definitions.note: a description of the people, standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: letters set wrong are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A debate over whether prophecies are murky, one side insisting they are plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: oracles were famous for ambiguous prophecies, like Delphi's.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient oracles such as Delphi gave notoriously ambiguous prophecies, so their forecasts are typically obscure.

clue.text: Where you might see nurses getting ahead

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: on hospital wards
second meaning: forward, further on

explanation.surface: Nurses are found in hospital as they advance in their careers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning reads the answer as two words, on wards, where nurses work.
explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward or ahead, continuing in the same direction.

clue.text: Worse-tempered knight and king overheard

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Sir is a knight's title
King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic monarch
the two words said together

explanation.surface: A grumpier knight and monarch are eavesdropped upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Surly means bad-tempered and grumpy, so surlier is the comparative, more ill-humoured.

clue.text: Thunder cracking with energy – if caught, you’ll get ill

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, letting its letters be reassembled

blocks.note: the fodder letters
E is the symbol for energy
anyone caught out in a thunderstorm is literally beneath the elements

explanation.surface: Get caught in a crackling, energetic thunderstorm and you'll fall sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives UNDER THE; the thunder itself is weather, and being caught in it puts you literally under it, a looser cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the weather is an idiom for feeling slightly unwell or ill.

clue.text: Land serious money

blocks.note: real as in 'a real problem', a serious one
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M2 money supply

explanation.surface: Getting a large sum of cash, or a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a verb, to secure; it is the noun, a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a land ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Brave Thomas?

blocks.note: first meaning: bold, robust, able to endure
second meaning: Thomas ..., the Victorian novelist and poet

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking whether someone named Thomas is brave; the question mark marks Thomas as an example of a famous bearer of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means bold and tough, and Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Queen follows procedure herself before she visits Covent Garden

blocks.note: op is short for operation, a surgical procedure
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
ago means in the past, before now
the Queen herself again, ER

explanation.surface: The Queen follows protocol before her own visit to Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' places the Queen after the procedure. The Royal Opera House stands in London's Covent Garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden is home to the Royal Opera House, so a woman visiting it is likely attending opera.

clue.text: Grain arranged as a bouquet?

indicators.note: arranged suggests putting things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Stalks of grain are arranged into a floral bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The bouquet is not flowers but bouquet garni, the bundle of herbs used in cooking; the question mark flags the culinary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Garni is French for garnished, and in a bouquet garni it follows the word bouquet as its descriptor.

clue.text: Spot man inside oil plant

indicators.note: one word placed inside another is held within it

blocks.note: to spot something is to see it
Sam is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone notices a worker inside an oil refinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil plant' reads as a refinery, but it is a plant grown for its oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a crop whose seeds are pressed to make sesame oil, so it is a plant yielding oil.

clue.text: Small chance he’ll paint your car

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
as in 'not a prayer', a chance of success

explanation.surface: There is little likelihood that he will repaint your car.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprayer is a person who applies paint with a spray gun, as in a garage respraying cars.
